project.name: @openmrs/esm-patient-management
project.description: Patient management microfrontend for the OpenMRS 3.x frontend

nodes.name: Service Queues
nodes.summary: Patient queue management including adding patients to queues, transition between queues and statuses, queue screen display, queue linelist tables, and queue administration. Covers the full lifecycle of a queue entry from creation through service completion.

businessRules: A visit is required before a patient can be added to a queue
Queue entry transitions create a history trail via the transition API
A queue entry can only be transitioned (ended + new started), not modified in place
Duplicate queue entries for the same patient in the same queue are prevented
Queue entry start time must not be prior to the previous queue entry's start time
Queue entry start time must not be in the future
crossDomainInteractions: Patients searched from Patient Search domain are added to queues
Queue entries reference patient visits from Active Visits domain
Patient banner shows queue entry status with priority indicator

nodes.name: Add Patient to Queue
nodes.summary: Searches for a patient, verifies they have an active visit, selects the queue service/location/priority, and creates a queue entry

nodes.name: Transition Queue Entry
nodes.summary: Moves a queue entry to a new queue, status, or priority via the transition API which ends the current entry and creates a new one with updated values. Includes undo capability.

nodes.name: Serve Queue Entry
nodes.summary: Marks a queue entry as being served by calling the patient to the service point, displayed as an active ticket on the queue screen with blinking status

nodes.name: Administer Queues and Rooms
nodes.summary: CRUD operations for managing queues and queue rooms, including creating, editing, retiring/deleting queues and queue rooms via the admin panel

nodes.name: Manage Queue Linelists
nodes.summary: Displays patient linelist tables per queue service with search, pagination, filtering, and action menus for queue entry operations

domainMeta.entryPoint: Route navigation to queue service table view

nodes.name: View Queue Metrics
nodes.summary: Displays checked-in patient counts, waiting patients, average wait time, and per-service metrics for queue monitoring

nodes.name: Open Create Queue Entry Workspace
nodes.summary: User clicks 'Add patient to queue' action, opening a workspace with patient search results

nodes.name: Select Patient and Verify Active Visit
nodes.summary: Patient banner is displayed showing patient details. The system verifies the patient has an active visit; if no active visit exists, a 'start visit' extension is shown as a prerequisite

nodes.name: Fill Queue Fields with Service, Priority, Status
nodes.summary: User selects queue service location, priority level, and status from configured options via radio buttons or combobox. Priority comment can be added

nodes.name: Submit Queue Entry via REST API
nodes.summary: POST request to /visit-queue-entry with visit UUID, queue UUID, priority, status, and patient UUID to create the queue entry

nodes.name: Handle Existing Visit Form
nodes.summary: If patient already has an active visit, presents the existing visit form that allows proceeding directly with queue entry creation using the existing visit

nodes.name: Open Queue Entry Action Modal
nodes.summary: User triggers a queue entry action (edit, move, transition) which opens a shared modal component with form fields for the operation

nodes.name: Select New Queue, Status, Priority and Transition Time
nodes.summary: User picks the target queue, new status, priority level, optional priority comment, and optionally modifies the transition date/time with validation

nodes.name: Call Queue Entry Transition API
nodes.summary: Sends a POST request to /queue-entry/transition ending the current queue entry and creating a new one with updated queue, status, or priority values

nodes.name: Handle Transition Errors and Refresh
nodes.summary: Handles duplicate queue entry errors, already-ended queue entry warnings, and other submission errors with appropriate snackbar notifications. Mutates SWR cache to refresh queue data

nodes.name: Undo Queue Entry Transition
nodes.summary: Sends a DELETE request to /queue-entry/transition to revert the most recent transition, restoring the previous queue entry state

nodes.name: Call Patient to Service Point
nodes.summary: Posts to /queueutil/assignticket with service point name, ticket number, and status to mark a ticket as being served

nodes.name: Display Active Tickets on Queue Screen
nodes.summary: Fetches active tickets with 3-second polling and displays them as cards showing ticket number, room, and blinking call status

nodes.name: Create and Edit Queues
nodes.summary: Admin panel for adding or editing queue definitions including service type, location, allowed priorities, and allowed statuses

nodes.name: Create and Edit Queue Rooms
nodes.summary: Admin panel for managing queue rooms with add, edit, and delete operations via forms and confirmation modals

nodes.name: Retire Queues and Queue Rooms
nodes.summary: Confirmation modals for retiring/deleting queues and queue rooms with loading states and error handling

nodes.name: View and Filter Queue Linelist
nodes.summary: Renders a reusable patient linelist table for a queue service with search, pagination, column sorting, and row-level actions

nodes.name: Execute Queue Entry Actions from Linelist
nodes.summary: Provides overflow menu on each linelist row with actions: call/serve, requeue, undo transition, void, edit, and clear all entries

nodes.name: Display Queue Metrics Cards
nodes.summary: Shows metrics cards with checked-in patient counts, average wait time, and service-specific statistics using SWR data fetching

nodes.name: Appointments
nodes.summary: Appointment scheduling and management including form-based creation/editing of appointments, calendar views, workload management, scheduled and unscheduled appointment lists, and patient appointment history.

businessRules: Appointment conflicts must be checked before saving
Appointments can be scheduled or unscheduled
Recurring appointment patterns can be defined
crossDomainInteractions: Patient registration provides patient data for appointment scheduling
Appointments appear on the home page dashboard via Appointment domain
Appointment metrics are displayed on the home page

nodes.name: Create or Edit Appointment
nodes.summary: Form-based appointment creation and editing with service selection, date/time picking, provider assignment, recurring patterns, and conflict checking

nodes.name: View Appointments Calendar
nodes.summary: Monthly calendar view of appointments with navigation between months and visualization of scheduled appointments per day

nodes.name: Manage Appointment Workload
nodes.summary: Monthly workload view showing provider appointment counts and capacity across services with visual workload indicators

nodes.name: View Patient Appointment History
nodes.summary: Displays a patient's appointment history including past and upcoming appointments with details and cancellation options

nodes.name: Fill Appointment Form
nodes.summary: User fills in appointment details: service type, date, time, provider, location, notes, and optional recurring pattern using react-hook-form with Zod validation

nodes.name: Check for Appointment Conflicts
nodes.summary: Validates proposed appointment time against existing appointments to detect scheduling conflicts before save

nodes.name: Save Appointment via REST API
nodes.summary: Posts the appointment payload to the server, handling both single and recurring appointments, then refreshes the appointment list

nodes.name: Cancel Existing Appointment
nodes.summary: Open cancel modal for an existing appointment, confirm cancellation, and update the appointment status

nodes.name: Navigate Monthly Calendar View
nodes.summary: Renders a monthly calendar grid with appointment indicators, month navigation, and service type filtering

nodes.name: View Monthly Provider Workload
nodes.summary: Displays workload cards for each service with appointment counts per provider, capacity tracking, and visual overload indicators

nodes.name: Active Visits
nodes.summary: Tracking and display of currently active patient visits with configurable data columns, visit summary details including encounters, medications, notes, and vital signs. Provides home page metrics tiles for active visit counts.

businessRules: Active visits are filtered by session location
Visit data includes configurable identifier and attribute columns
Visit summaries include encounters, diagnoses, vitals, medications and notes
crossDomainInteractions: Queue entries are associated with active visits from this domain
Active visit counts appear on the home page dashboard tiles

nodes.name: View Active Visits Table
nodes.summary: Displays a paginated, sortable table of currently active visits at the user's session location with configurable identifier, attribute, and observation columns

domainMeta.entryPoint: Route navigation to active visits widget

nodes.name: View Visit Summary
nodes.summary: Displays detailed visit summary with encounters, diagnoses, medications, notes, vitals, and test results in organized tabbed views

domainMeta.entryPoint: Click on a visit in the active visits table

nodes.name: Fetch Active Visits from API
nodes.summary: Uses SWR infinite query to fetch active visits with custom representation including patient identifiers, person attributes, and flattened observation data

nodes.name: Render Sortable Active Visits Table
nodes.summary: Renders a data table with configurable columns for identifiers, attributes, observations, name, gender, age, visit type, and visit time with sort functionality

nodes.name: Display Visit Encounters and Details
nodes.summary: Renders visit detail overview with encounter list, diagnosis display, medication administration, clinical notes, and vitals in organized sections

nodes.name: Patient Registration
nodes.summary: Patient registration workflow including creation of new patients and editing existing patient records. Covers form fields for name, demographics, address, identifiers, relationships, death info, and patient photo capture.

businessRules: Patient identifiers must be unique and validated against identifier types
Registration can be done online or offline with queued synchronization
Form validation uses configurable validation schemas per field type
Address fields have hierarchical dependencies
crossDomainInteractions: Registered patients become searchable via the Patient Search domain
Patient banner in Patient Search displays registration data

nodes.name: Register New Patient
nodes.summary: Creates a new patient record by filling out registration sections (name, demographics, address, identifiers, relationships), capturing a photo, and submitting via Formik-managed form with validation

domainMeta.entryPoint: Route navigation to registration form or 'Add Patient' link

nodes.name: Edit Existing Patient
nodes.summary: Loads an existing patient's data into the registration form, allowing updates to demographics, address, identifiers, relationships, and other configurable sections

domainMeta.entryPoint: Route navigation to registration form with patient UUID parameter

nodes.name: Fill Registration Sections
nodes.summary: User completes configurable sections: demographics (name, gender, DOB), address, identifier, relationships, and death info using field components for each data type

nodes.name: Validate Registration Form
nodes.summary: Applies validation schemas per field including required fields, date formats, identifier patterns, and cross-field validations

nodes.name: Submit Patient via Save Patient Transaction Manager
nodes.summary: Executes a transaction manager that creates patient, person name, identifiers, address, attributes, relationships, encounters, and photo via REST API calls

nodes.name: Handle Offline Registration
nodes.summary: When offline, serializes the patient registration as a sync item for later synchronization to the server

nodes.name: Patient Search
nodes.summary: Patient search functionality with compact search bar, advanced search page with filters, patient banner display with contact details, and start-visit workflow. Supports searching by name, identifier, or advanced criteria.

businessRules: Search uses configured search API with custom representation
Patient banner can show queue status from Service Queues domain
crossDomainInteractions: Patient search results can launch registration edit flow
Patient search is the entry point for adding patients to queues
Search results display patient banner from this domain

nodes.name: Search for Patient
nodes.summary: Initiates a patient search via compact search bar or advanced search page with filters, displaying results with patient banner and contact details

domainMeta.entryPoint: Search bar or advanced search page route

nodes.name: Enter Search Query
nodes.summary: User types a patient name or identifier into the search bar, triggering real-time autocomplete search results

nodes.name: View Advanced Search Results with Filters
nodes.summary: User navigates to the advanced search page with additional filter options and views paginated search results

nodes.name: Display Patient Banner
nodes.summary: Shows patient banner with photo, name, identifiers, age, gender, contact details toggling, and queue status indicator

nodes.name: Patient Lists
nodes.summary: Cohort-based patient list management with CRUD operations for lists, add/remove member functionality, list dashboard with search and pagination, and offline support for synchronized patient lists.

businessRules: Patient lists are implemented as OpenMRS cohorts via /cohortm REST API
Lists can be created as user-defined system cohorts
Lists support offline data synchronization
crossDomainInteractions: Patients can be added to lists from the Patient Search result actions
Patient list members are individual patient records

nodes.name: Create and Manage Patient Lists
nodes.summary: Create new patient lists, edit existing list metadata, delete/retire lists, and view lists dashboard with searching and pagination

nodes.name: Manage List Membership
nodes.summary: Add patients to a list and remove patients from a list with confirmation modals, list detail view with member table

domainMeta.entryPoint: Overflow menu on patient search results or list detail page

nodes.name: Create New Patient List
nodes.summary: User fills out name, description, and type for a new patient list via the patient list form, which creates a cohort via REST API

nodes.name: View and Manage Lists Dashboard
nodes.summary: Lists dashboard with search, pagination, and action menus for editing or deleting lists

nodes.name: Edit or Delete Patient List
nodes.summary: Edit list name and description, or delete/retire a patient list with confirmation modal

nodes.name: Add Patient to List
nodes.summary: Select a patient and add them to one or more patient lists via an overlay modal trigger from the patient search overflow menu

nodes.name: Remove Patient from List
nodes.summary: Remove a patient from a list with confirmation modal from the list detail view

nodes.name: Bed Management
nodes.summary: Administration and summary views for hospital beds including bed creation/editing, bed types (CRUD), bed tags (CRUD), ward-to-bed assignments, and bed summary dashboards.

businessRules: Beds are associated with wards and have types and tags
Bed tags and types are configurable through admin forms
Bed administration requires form-based creation with resource lookups
crossDomainInteractions: Ward domain uses bed data for inpatient bed assignments
Bed availability provides data for bed summary views

nodes.name: Administer Beds
nodes.summary: Create, edit, and manage beds including bed type and bed tag configuration, and bed-to-ward assignment via form-based workspace

domainMeta.entryPoint: Bed administration route and admin forms

nodes.name: View Bed Summary
nodes.summary: Dashboard showing bed occupancy summary across wards, bed type distribution, and bed tag groupings

nodes.name: Create or Edit Bed
nodes.summary: Form workspace for creating or editing a bed with ward assignment, bed type, bed tag selection, row/column positioning, and status

nodes.name: Manage Bed Types
nodes.summary: CRUD operations for bed types including create new, edit existing, and delete with confirmation, displayed in an administration table

nodes.name: Manage Bed Tags
nodes.summary: CRUD operations for bed tags including create new tag form, edit existing tag, and delete with confirmation modal

nodes.name: Display Ward and Bed Summary
nodes.summary: Renders summary view with bed counts per ward, occupancy status, and bed type/tag distribution cards

nodes.name: Ward
nodes.summary: Inpatient ward management including ward view with bed layouts, patient admissions, discharges, transfers, bed-to-patient assignments, admission requests, patient notes, and maternal ward with mother-baby linking.

businessRules: Admission creates an encounter with admission encounter type
Transfer creates an encounter with transfer-within-hospital encounter type
Discharge ends the inpatient stay
Beds can be shared by multiple patients (e.g., maternal ward with newborns)
Admission requests must be approved before bed assignment
crossDomainInteractions: Ward uses Bed Management domain data for bed layouts
Patient data comes from the core patient model
Encounter creation connects to the OpenMRS encounter/visit system

nodes.name: Admit Patient to Ward
nodes.summary: Admits a patient to the ward by assigning them to a bed, creating an admission encounter, and updating the ward view

domainMeta.entryPoint: Admit patient button in ward workspace

nodes.name: Transfer or Discharge Patient
nodes.summary: Transfers a patient to a different bed/ward or discharges them, creating appropriate encounter types and updating bed assignments

domainMeta.entryPoint: Transfer or discharge action buttons in ward workspace

nodes.name: View Ward
nodes.summary: Displays the ward view with bed layouts, patient cards on beds, admission requests, and ward-level metrics (patient count, newborns, females of reproductive age)

nodes.name: Assign Bed and Create Admission Encounter
nodes.summary: Selects an available bed for the patient, creates an admission encounter via POST /encounter, and assigns the patient to the bed layout

nodes.name: Handle Admission Request
nodes.summary: Processes pending admission requests, allowing approval and bed assignment through the admission request workspace

nodes.name: Create Transfer Encounter
nodes.summary: Creates a transfer-within-hospital encounter and moves the patient to a new bed in the destination ward

nodes.name: Discharge Patient
nodes.summary: Creates a discharge encounter and removes the patient from the bed layout, ending the inpatient stay

nodes.name: Display Ward Layout with Beds
nodes.summary: Renders the ward view showing all beds with occupancy status, patient cards, and empty bed indicators arranged by row and column

nodes.name: Compute Ward Metrics
nodes.summary: Calculates ward metrics including total patient count, newborn count, females of reproductive age count from the ward patient group data

nodes.name: Display Maternal Ward View
nodes.summary: Special ward view for maternal ward with mother-baby bed sharing, where mothers and newborns can occupy the same bed

nodes.name: Home and Dashboard
nodes.summary: Home page dashboard container and navigation menu configuration. Provides sidebar navigation and renders extension-based dashboard views for all registered microfrontend domains. Acts as the shell for the entire application.

businessRules: Dashboards are registered as extensions to the homepage-dashboard-slot
Active dashboard is determined by URL parameter or defaults to first registered dashboard
Sidebar mode can be configured as normal or minimized
crossDomainInteractions: All domain dashboards (queues, appointments, visits, etc.) are rendered inside this container
Navigation to all domains flows through the home page side menu

nodes.name: Navigate Dashboard
nodes.summary: Loads the dashboard container, resolves the active dashboard from URL params, renders sidebar navigation, and delegates rendering to the active microfrontend extension

nodes.name: Resolve and Render Active Dashboard
nodes.summary: Reads URL parameters to determine the active dashboard extension, displays sidebar navigation, and renders the corresponding dashboard slot

nodes.name: Render Sidebar Menu
nodes.summary: Renders the side menu with navigation links to all registered dashboard extensions based on configuration

edges.description: Patient search results are used to select patients for queue entry creation
Queue entries require patient active visits for creation and display visit data
Patient search can navigate to edit patient registration
Ward view uses bed layouts and bed types managed by the Bed Management domain
Patients can be added to lists from patient search overflow menu
Home dashboard renders the service queues dashboard extension
Home dashboard renders the appointments dashboard extension
Home dashboard renders the active visits dashboard extension and metric tiles
Appointment form uses patient data fetched via patient UUID
